Q. 4 (ii) The sample correlation coefficient R is a point estimator of the population correlation coefficient rho.

True

Q. 4 (iii) The correlation coefficient r is not symmetrical with respect to X and Y.

False

Q. 4 (iv) The correlation coefficient changes with a change in origin.

False

Q. 4 (vi) The correlation coefficient is not independent of the origin and the unit of measurement.

False

Q. 4 (xiii, as printed) The correlation coefficient r always lies between -1 and 1.

True

Q. 4 (xiv, as printed) r = 1 indicates perfect positive correlation between the two variables and slope is positive.

True

Q. 4 (xv, as printed) r = -1 indicates perfect negative correlation between the two variables and slope is negative.

True

Q. 5 (i) r = 0 indicates that one regression line is horizontal and the other regression line is vertical.

True

Q. 5 (ii) The correlation coefficient r is the geometric mean of the two regression coefficients.

True

Q. 5 (iii) Each of the two estimated regression lines passes through the point (x-bar, y-bar).

True

Q. 5 (iv) We can always estimate the X and Y values from the regression equation of Y on X.

False

Q. 5 (v) The regression coefficient of X on Y is -1.2 and of Y on X is 0.3.

False

Q. 5 (vi) The regression coefficient of X on Y is -1.2 and of Y on X is -0.3.

True

Q. 5 (vii) The regression coefficient of X on Y, regression coefficient of Y on X and correlation coefficient have same sign.

True

Q. 5 (viii) If the regression coefficient of X on Y is -1.2 and of Y on X is -0.3, the correlation coefficient is 0.6.

False

Q. 5 (ix) The regression coefficient of X on Y is always equal to the regression coefficient of Y on X.

False

options: The expected value of the independent variable for a given value of the dependent variable
The expected value of the dependent random variable for a given value of the independent non-random variable
A set of points representing observed pairs of values
The estimates a and b obtained by least squares
mcqs.q: Regression is a relationship that describes the dependence of which quantity?
mcqs.why: Objective Q.1(i) in the notes states exactly this definition of regression: the dependence of the expected value of the dependent random variable for a given value of the independent non-random variable.

mcqs.q: The variable that forms the basis of estimation or prediction is called what?
mcqs.why: Objective Q.1(ii) states that the variable forming the basis of estimation is the regressor. The regressand, in Q.1(iii), is the variable whose resulting value depends upon the selected value of the independent variable.

options: Four parameters: alpha, beta, mu_(Y|x) and sigma-squared
Two parameters: alpha and beta only
Three parameters: alpha, beta and r
mcqs.q: According to the objective questions, the simple linear regression model contains which parameters?
mcqs.why: The notes mark the statement that the model contains two parameters alpha and beta as False, and the statement that it contains four parameters alpha, beta, mu_(Y|x) and sigma-squared as True.

options: Alpha is the slope and beta is the intercept
Alpha is the regression coefficient and beta is the intercept
Alpha is the y-intercept and beta is the slope
Alpha and beta are both intercepts
mcqs.q: In the regression line, what are the roles of alpha and beta?
mcqs.why: The notes mark as False the swapped statement that alpha is the slope and beta is the intercept. They mark as True that alpha is the y-intercept, and that the constant b estimates beta representing the slope.

options: The sum of the residuals should be the greatest possible
The sum of squares of the residuals of observed values from their corresponding estimated values should be the least possible
The sum of the residuals should equal the sum of squares of the residuals
The correlation coefficient should be independent of origin and scale
mcqs.q: What does the principle of least squares say?
mcqs.why: Objective Q.2(viii) states this principle as True, and Q.2(ix) adds that the principle of least squares is used for finding the estimates a and b of the parameters alpha and beta.

options: r is not symmetrical with respect to X and Y
r changes with a change in origin
r is not independent of the origin and the unit of measurement
r is symmetrical with respect to X and Y and is independent of origin and unit of measurement
mcqs.q: Which statement about the correlation coefficient r is correct?
mcqs.why: The notes mark each of the first three statements as False: r is not asymmetrical, r does not change with origin, and r is not dependent on origin and unit. Hence r is symmetrical in X and Y and independent of origin and unit.

options: Perfect positive correlation between the two variables and slope is positive
Perfect negative correlation between the two variables and slope is negative
The two variables are linearly independent
One regression line is horizontal and the other is vertical
mcqs.q: What does r = 1 indicate?
mcqs.why: The notes mark as True that r = 1 indicates perfect positive correlation and the slope is positive, while r = -1 indicates perfect negative correlation. Also, r always lies between -1 and 1.

options: Both regression lines coincide with each other
Both regression lines have the same positive slope
One regression line is horizontal and the other regression line is vertical
Both regression lines pass through the origin
mcqs.q: If r = 0, what is true about the two regression lines?
mcqs.why: Objective Q.5(i) is marked True in the notes: r = 0 indicates that one regression line is horizontal and the other regression line is vertical. The notes also state separately that r = 0 indicates the variables are linearly independent.

mcqs.q: The regression coefficient of X on Y is -1.2 and the regression coefficient of Y on X is -0.3. What is the correlation coefficient r?
mcqs.why: Working: r is the geometric mean of the two regression coefficients, so r-squared = b_xy x b_yx = (-1.2) x (-0.3) = 0.36, giving |r| = 0.6. The coefficients, b_xy, b_yx and r have the same sign, which is negative here, so r = -0.6. The notes mark the value 0.6 as False for this case.

options: The value of X for every given value of Y
The correlation coefficient from the slope alone
Both X and Y values in all cases
The mean value of Y for a given value of x
mcqs.q: What is the estimated regression equation of Y on x used to estimate?
mcqs.why: Objective Q.2(xii) is marked True: the estimated regression equation of Y on x is used to estimate the mean value of Y for a given value of x. The notes mark as False the claim that X and Y can always be estimated from this one equation.

lessons.title: Exercise — Short Questions
lessons.notes_html:
What is association between two attributes?

Two attributes are associated when they are not independent of each other.

Association is studied from a contingency table of observed frequencies.

The coefficient of association, denoted by Q, measures association between two attributes.

What is the chi-square test of independence?

It measures the discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies.

The value of the chi-square statistic is always non-negative.

Rejection of H0 of independence indicates that the two criteria of classification are associated.

mcqs.q: When are two attributes said to be associated?
options: When they are independent of each other
When they are not independent of each other
When they are measured in quantity only
When their frequencies are all equal
mcqs.why: The notes define association directly: two attributes are associated when they are not independent of each other.

mcqs.q: Association between two attributes is studied from which table?
options: A table of expected frequencies only
A contingency table of observed frequencies
A table of class intervals only
mcqs.why: The notes state that association is studied from a contingency table of observed frequencies.

mcqs.q: What does the coefficient denoted by Q measure?
options: Discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies
mcqs.why: The notes state that the coefficient of association, denoted by Q, measures association between two attributes.

mcqs.q: What does the chi-square test of independence measure?
options: The sum of all observed frequencies
The discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies
The product of two class frequencies
mcqs.why: The notes define the chi-square test of independence as measuring the discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the value of the chi-square statistic is correct?
options: It can be any positive or negative value
It is always equal to zero
mcqs.why: The notes state explicitly that the value of the chi-square statistic is always non-negative, so it can never be negative.

mcqs.q: What does rejection of H0 of independence indicate?
options: The two criteria of classification are independent
The two criteria of classification are associated
The observed frequencies are all zero
The coefficient Q cannot be calculated
mcqs.why: The notes state that rejection of H0 of independence indicates that the two criteria of classification are associated.

mcqs.q: In the chi-square test of independence, H0 is the hypothesis of what?
options: Equal class frequencies in every class
mcqs.why: The notes refer to H0 as the hypothesis of independence, whose rejection indicates association between the criteria.

mcqs.q: Which two kinds of frequencies are compared in the chi-square test of independence?
mcqs.why: The chi-square test measures the discrepancy between observed frequencies and expected frequencies, as stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: Which symbol is used in the notes for the coefficient of association?
mcqs.why: The notes denote the coefficient of association by Q, which measures association between two attributes.

mcqs.q: If two attributes are independent of each other, how are they described in terms of association?
mcqs.why: Association is defined as not being independent, so independent attributes are not associated with each other.

lessons.title: Exercise — True or False
lessons.notes_html:
The two attributes A and B are associated, if (AB) = (A)(B) divided by n.

False

The coefficient of association, denoted by Q, is a measure of association between the two attributes.

True

The coefficient of association always lies between -1 and 1.

True

A measure of the discrepancy between the observed and expected frequencies is called a chi-square test of independence.

True

The value of chi-square statistic is always non-negative.

True

The rejection of H0 of independence indicates that two criteria of classification are associated.

True

mcqs.q: Judge this statement: 'The two attributes A and B are associated if (AB) = (A)(B) / n.'
options: True, because equality is the condition for association
False, because equality is the condition for independence
True, because Q is then equal to 1
False, because (AB) can never equal (A)(B) / n
mcqs.why: The notes mark this statement False: (AB) = (A)(B) / n is the independence condition, not the association condition.

mcqs.q: Judge this statement: 'The coefficient of association, denoted by Q, is a measure of association between the two attributes.'
options: True only when Q is negative
True only for variables, not attributes
mcqs.why: The notes mark this statement True: Q, the coefficient of association, measures association between two attributes.

mcqs.q: Judge this statement: 'The coefficient of association always lies between -1 and 1.'
options: False, it lies between 0 and 1 only
mcqs.why: The notes mark this statement True: the coefficient of association Q always lies between -1 and 1 inclusive.

mcqs.q: Judge this statement: 'A measure of the discrepancy between the observed and expected frequencies is called a chi-square test of independence.'
options: False, it is called Yule's coefficient
mcqs.why: The notes mark this statement True: the discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies is measured by the chi-square test.

mcqs.q: Judge this statement: 'The value of the chi-square statistic is always non-negative.'
options: True only in a 2 x 2 table
mcqs.why: The notes mark this statement True: the chi-square statistic is always non-negative and can never take a negative value.

mcqs.q: Judge this statement: 'Rejection of H0 of independence indicates that two criteria of classification are associated.'
mcqs.why: The notes mark this statement True: rejecting H0 of independence means the two criteria of classification are associated.

mcqs.q: The condition (AB) = (A)(B) / n is the condition for which situation?
mcqs.why: Under independence (AB) / n = ((A) / n) x ((B) / n), which rearranges to (AB) = (A)(B) / n, so equality means independence.

mcqs.q: Which of the following values is impossible for the coefficient of association Q?
mcqs.why: Q always lies between -1 and 1, so 1.5 is impossible, while 0, -1 and -0.5 all lie inside the allowed range.

mcqs.q: Which of the following values is impossible for a chi-square statistic?
mcqs.why: The chi-square statistic is always non-negative, so -5 is impossible, whereas 0 and positive values such as 4.79 are possible.

mcqs.q: The chi-square test of independence is a measure of the discrepancy between which frequencies?
mcqs.why: The notes state that the chi-square test of independence measures the discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies.

lessons.title: Exercise 15.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q. 1 (a) Distinguish between attribute and variable. Define positive classes, negative classes and ultimate classes.

Step 1: An attribute is a characteristic which varies only in quality from one individual to another, for example marital status, blindness or smoking; a variable is a characteristic which varies in quantity, for example height or weight.

Step 2: A class represented by positive attributes only is a positive class, for example A, B and AB; a class represented by negative attributes only is a negative class, for example alpha, beta and alpha beta; a class represented by both positive and negative attributes is a contrary class, for example A beta and alpha B.

Answer: The frequencies of the classes of the highest order are called ultimate class frequencies. For two attributes A and B the ultimate classes are AB, A beta, alpha B and alpha beta; their number is 2 to the power k for k attributes.

Q. 1 (b) Given the ultimate class frequencies (AB) = 95, (A beta) = 55, (alpha B) = 85, (alpha beta) = 45, find the frequencies of the positive and negative classes and the whole number of observations n.

Step 1: (A) = (AB) + (A beta) = 95 + 55 = 150.

Step 2: (B) = (AB) + (alpha B) = 95 + 85 = 180.

Step 3: (alpha) = (alpha B) + (alpha beta) = 85 + 45 = 130.

Step 4: (beta) = (A beta) + (alpha beta) = 55 + 45 = 100.

Answer: n = 95 + 55 + 85 + 45 = 280; (A) = 150, (B) = 180, (alpha) = 130, (beta) = 100, as printed in the book.

Q. 2 (a) Given n = 250, (A) = 80, (B) = 100, (AB) = 70, find the frequencies of the ultimate classes.

Step 1: (A beta) = (A) - (AB) = 80 - 70 = 10.

Step 2: (alpha B) = (B) - (AB) = 100 - 70 = 30.

Step 3: (alpha beta) = n - (A) - (B) + (AB) = 250 - 80 - 100 + 70 = 140.

Answer: (A beta) = 10, (alpha B) = 30, (alpha beta) = 140, with (AB) = 70, as printed in the book.

Q. 2 (b) Measurements are made on a thousand husbands and a thousand wives. If the measurements of husbands exceed the measurements of the wives in 800 cases for one measurement, in 700 cases for another, and in 660 cases for both measurements, in how many cases will both the measurements on the wife exceed the measurement on the husband?

Step 1: Let H1 be the set where the husband exceeds the wife in the first measurement (800 cases) and H2 the set for the second measurement (700 cases); both together occur in 660 cases.

Step 2: Cases where the husband exceeds the wife in at least one measurement = 800 + 700 - 660 = 840.

Step 3: The remaining cases, where the wife exceeds the husband in both measurements, = 1000 - 840 = 160.

Answer: 160 cases, as printed in the book.

Q. 2 (c) Given that (A) = (alpha) = (B) = (beta) = n/2, show that (i) (AB) = (alpha beta) and (ii) (A beta) = (alpha B).

Step 1: (AB) + (A beta) = (A) = n/2 and (AB) + (alpha B) = (B) = n/2, so (A beta) = (alpha B). This proves (ii).

Step 2: (alpha beta) + (alpha B) = (alpha) = n/2 and (AB) + (alpha B) = (B) = n/2, so (alpha beta) = (AB). This proves (i).

Answer: Both equalities follow from the four given class frequencies.

Q. 3 (a) Define the consistence of the data.

Step 1: Class frequencies observed in one and the same population are said to be consistent if they conform with one another and do not conflict with each other.

Step 2: No class frequency can ever be negative, so the necessary and sufficient condition for consistence is that no ultimate class frequency should be negative.

Answer: To test consistence, calculate the ultimate class frequencies from the given data; if any one of them is negative the data are inconsistent, and if none is negative the data are consistent.

Q. 3 (b) Find whether the data given below in each case are consistent: (i) n = 120, (A) = 82, (AB) = 90; (ii) n = 50, (A) = 40, (B) = 32, (AB) = 15; (iii) n = 1000, (AB) = 200, (A beta) = 350, (alpha B) = 500.

Step 1 (i): (A beta) = (A) - (AB) = 82 - 90 = -8, which is negative.

Step 2 (ii): (alpha beta) = n - (A) - (B) + (AB) = 50 - 40 - 32 + 15 = -7, which is negative.

Step 3 (iii): (alpha beta) = n - (AB) - (A beta) - (alpha B) = 1000 - 200 - 350 - 500 = -50, which is negative.

Answer: (i), (ii) and (iii) are all NOT consistent, since an ultimate class frequency is negative in each case (-8, -7 and -50 respectively), as printed in the book.

Q. 3 (c) Comment on the following data contained in a report: 100 students appeared in a test of whom 80 passed in Statistics, 70 passed in Mathematics and 48 passed in both the subjects.

Step 1: Let A be passing Statistics and B passing Mathematics, so (A) = 80, (B) = 70, (AB) = 48 and n = 100.

Step 2: (alpha beta) = n - (A) - (B) + (AB) = 100 - 80 - 70 + 48 = -2, which is negative.

Answer: Not consistent, since (alpha beta) = -2, as printed in the book.

Q. 4 (a) What is meant by independence of attributes?

Step 1: Two attributes A and B are independent if the proportion of individuals possessing both attributes equals the product of the proportions possessing each attribute separately.

Step 2: In class frequencies this is (AB) / n = ((A) / n) x ((B) / n), that is (AB) = (A)(B) / n.

Answer: Under independence the 2 x 2 table is completely determined by (A), (B) and n; any departure from (AB) = (A)(B) / n means the attributes are associated.

Q. 4 (b) There are 240 A's and 270 B's in 600 observations. What would be the number of AB if A and B are independent?

Step 1: Under independence (AB) = (A)(B) / n = (240)(270) / 600.

Step 2: (240)(270) = 64800, and 64800 / 600 = 108.

Answer: (AB) = 108, as printed in the book.

Q. 4 (c) If A's are 60% and B's are 40% of the whole number of observations, what must be the percentage of AB's in order that we conclude that A and B are independent?

Step 1: Take n = 100, so (A) = 60 and (B) = 40.

Step 2: Under independence (AB) = (A)(B) / n = (60)(40) / 100 = 24.

Answer: There must be 24% AB's, as printed in the book.

Q. 5 (a) When are two attributes independent, positively associated, negatively associated?

Step 1: The attributes are independent if (AB) = (A)(B) / n; then Yule's coefficient of association Q = 0.

Step 2: They are positively associated (or simply associated) if (AB) > (A)(B) / n; then Q > 0.

Answer: They are negatively associated (or disassociated) if (AB) < (A)(B) / n; then Q < 0. Complete association gives Q = 1 and complete disassociation gives Q = -1.

Q. 5 (b) Given the following data, determine the nature of association between the attributes A and B: (i) (A) = 30, (B) = 60, (AB) = 12, n = 150; (ii) (AB) = 110, (alpha B) = 90, (A beta) = 290, (alpha beta) = 510; (iii) (A) = 415, (AB) = 147, (alpha) = 285, (alpha beta) = 170.

Step 1 (i): Expected (AB) under independence = (30)(60) / 150 = 12, which equals the observed 12.

Step 2 (ii): (A) = 110 + 290 = 400, (B) = 110 + 90 = 200, n = 1000, so expected (AB) = (400)(200) / 1000 = 80, which is less than the observed 110.

Step 3 (iii): (alpha B) = (alpha) - (alpha beta) = 285 - 170 = 115, so (B) = 147 + 115 = 262 and n = 415 + 285 = 700; expected (AB) = (415)(262) / 700 = 155.33, which is greater than the observed 147.

Answer: (i) Independent, (ii) Positively associated, (iii) Negatively associated, as printed in the book.

Q. 6 (a) What is meant by association of attributes?

Step 1: Two attributes A and B are said to be associated if they are not independent, that is if (AB) is not equal to (A)(B) / n.

Step 2: Association is studied from a contingency table of observed frequencies, and its strength is measured by Yule's coefficient Q, which lies between -1 and +1.

Answer: Association means that the presence of one attribute changes the chance of the other attribute being present; it is the attribute analogue of correlation between variables.

Q. 6 (b) Explain the difference between the following with examples: (i) Attribute and variable, (ii) Correlation and association, (iii) Positive association and negative association.

Step 1 (i): An attribute varies only in quality (for example, blind or not blind, married or unmarried), while a variable varies in quantity (for example, height in centimetres or income in rupees).

Step 2 (ii): Correlation measures the linear relationship between two variables and is measured by the correlation coefficient r; association measures the relationship between two attributes and is measured by Q or tested by chi-square.

Answer (iii): Positive association means (AB) > (A)(B) / n, so the attributes tend to occur together (for example, vaccination and exemption from attack would be positively associated if the vaccinated escaped attack); negative association means (AB) < (A)(B) / n, so one attribute tends to exclude the other.

Q. 7 (a) Find the association between injection against typhoid and exemption from attack from the following contingency table: Inoculated - Attacked 528, Not attacked 25; Not inoculated - Attacked 790, Not attacked 175.

Step 1: Let A be inoculated and B be attacked, so (AB) = 528, (A beta) = 25, (alpha B) = 790, (alpha beta) = 175.

Step 2: Q = ((AB)(alpha beta) - (A beta)(alpha B)) / ((AB)(alpha beta) + (A beta)(alpha B)) = ((528)(175) - (25)(790)) / ((528)(175) + (25)(790)).

Step 3: (528)(175) = 92400 and (25)(790) = 19750, so Q = (92400 - 19750) / (92400 + 19750) = 72650 / 112150 = 0.65.

Answer: Q = 0.65, as printed in the book; with A = inoculated and B = attacked, the positive value means inoculation and attack are positively associated in this table.

Q. 7 (b) Calculate the coefficient of the association between the intelligence of fathers and sons in the following data: Intelligent fathers with intelligent sons = 265; Intelligent fathers with dull sons = 100; Dull fathers with intelligent sons = 95; Dull fathers with dull sons = 450.

Step 1: (AB) = 265, (A beta) = 100, (alpha B) = 95, (alpha beta) = 450.

Step 2: Q = ((265)(450) - (100)(95)) / ((265)(450) + (100)(95)) = (119250 - 9500) / (119250 + 9500).

Step 3: Q = 109750 / 128750 = 0.85.

Answer: Q = 0.85, as printed in the book; intelligence of fathers and sons is strongly positively associated.

Q. 7 (c) Find if there is any association between the tempers of brothers and sisters from the following data: Good natured brothers and good natured sisters = 1230; Good natured brothers and sullen sisters = 850; Sullen brothers and good natured sisters = 530; Sullen brothers and sullen sisters = 980.

Step 1: (AB) = 1230, (A beta) = 850, (alpha B) = 530, (alpha beta) = 980.

Step 2: Q = ((1230)(980) - (850)(530)) / ((1230)(980) + (850)(530)) = (1205400 - 450500) / (1205400 + 450500).

Step 3: Q = 754900 / 1655900 = 0.46.

Answer: Q = 0.46, as printed in the book; the tempers of brothers and sisters are positively associated.

Q. 8 (a) 750 students appeared in an examination and 470 were successful. 465 had attended classes and 58 of them failed. Calculate the coefficient of association to discuss association between attending classes and success.

Step 1: Let A be attending classes and B success. Attended and successful = 465 - 58 = 407, so (AB) = 407 and (A beta) = 58.

Step 2: Not attended = 750 - 465 = 285; successful among them = 470 - 407 = 63, so (alpha B) = 63 and (alpha beta) = 285 - 63 = 222.

Step 3: Q = ((407)(222) - (58)(63)) / ((407)(222) + (58)(63)) = (90354 - 3654) / (90354 + 3654) = 86700 / 94008 = 0.92.

Answer: Q = 0.92, highly positive association, as printed in the book; attending classes is strongly associated with success.

Q. 8 (b) 100 students appeared in an examination, and 50 failed in Mathematics, 60 failed in Statistics and 40 failed in both. Find if there is any association between the failing in Mathematics and Statistics.

Step 1: Let A be failing Mathematics and B failing Statistics, so (AB) = 40, (A beta) = 50 - 40 = 10, (alpha B) = 60 - 40 = 20, (alpha beta) = 100 - 50 - 60 + 40 = 30.

Step 2: Q = ((40)(30) - (10)(20)) / ((40)(30) + (10)(20)) = (1200 - 200) / (1200 + 200) = 1000 / 1400 = 0.71.

Answer: Q = 0.71, as printed in the book; failing in Mathematics and failing in Statistics are positively associated.

Q. 8 (c) Can vaccination be regarded as preventive measure for small pox from the following data: Of 1482 persons in a locality exposed to small pox, 368 in all were attacked. Of 1482 persons, 343 persons had been vaccinated and of these 35 were attacked.

Step 1: Let A be vaccinated and B attacked, so (AB) = 35, (A beta) = 343 - 35 = 308, (alpha B) = 368 - 35 = 333, (alpha beta) = 1482 - 343 - 333 = 806.

Step 2: Q = ((35)(806) - (308)(333)) / ((35)(806) + (308)(333)) = (28210 - 102564) / (28210 + 102564) = -74354 / 130774 = -0.57.

Answer: Q = -0.57, as printed in the book. The negative association between vaccination and attack means the vaccinated were attacked much less often, so vaccination can be regarded as a preventive measure.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an attribute rather than a variable?
mcqs.why: An attribute varies only in quality, for example marital status, blindness or smoking; height and weight vary in quantity and are variables.

mcqs.q: Given (AB) = 95, (A beta) = 55, (alpha B) = 85 and (alpha beta) = 45, what is (A)?
mcqs.why: Working: (A) = (AB) + (A beta) = 95 + 55 = 150, adding the two ultimate classes that contain attribute A.

mcqs.q: Given n = 250, (A) = 80, (B) = 100 and (AB) = 70, what is (alpha beta)?
mcqs.why: Working: (alpha beta) = n - (A) - (B) + (AB) = 250 - 80 - 100 + 70 = 140, as obtained in the notes.

mcqs.q: Husbands exceed wives in 800 cases for one measurement, 700 for another and 660 for both, out of 1000 couples. In how many cases does the wife exceed the husband in both measurements?
mcqs.why: Working: husband exceeds in at least one = 800 + 700 - 660 = 840, so wife exceeds in both = 1000 - 840 = 160 cases.

mcqs.q: What is the necessary and sufficient condition for the consistence of data?
options: Every ultimate class frequency must be zero
No ultimate class frequency should be negative
mcqs.why: No class frequency can ever be negative, so data are consistent exactly when no ultimate class frequency is negative.

mcqs.q: For n = 120, (A) = 82 and (AB) = 90, are the data consistent?
options: Yes, because (AB) is the largest frequency
No, because n is too small
mcqs.why: Working: (A beta) = (A) - (AB) = 82 - 90 = -8, which is negative, so an ultimate frequency is negative and the data are not consistent.

mcqs.q: There are 240 A's and 270 B's in 600 observations. If A and B are independent, what is (AB)?
mcqs.why: Working: under independence (AB) = (A)(B) / n = (240)(270) / 600 = 64800 / 600 = 108.

mcqs.q: If A's are 60% and B's are 40% of all observations, what percentage must AB's be for A and B to be independent?
Given (A) = 30, (B) = 60, (AB) = 12 and n = 150, what is the nature of association between A and B?
mcqs.why: Working: expected (AB) under independence = (A)(B) / n = (30)(60) / 150 = 1800 / 150 = 12, equal to the observed 12, so A and B are independent.

mcqs.q: Intelligent fathers and sons: (AB) = 265, (A beta) = 100, (alpha B) = 95, (alpha beta) = 450. What is Yule's Q?

lessons.title: Exercise 15.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q. 1 (a) Define contingency table and cell frequency. What is a 2 x 2 contingency table?

Step 1: A contingency table is a table of observed frequencies in which the observations are classified according to two criteria, with rows for the categories of one attribute and columns for the categories of the other.

Step 2: The frequency in any one cell of the table, that is the number of observations falling in one particular row and column combination, is the cell frequency; row totals and column totals are the marginal frequencies.

Answer: A 2 x 2 contingency table is the table for two attributes each with two categories, giving the four ultimate class frequencies (AB), (A beta), (alpha B) and (alpha beta), with total n.

Q. 1 (b) In an investigation into eye-colour and left or right handedness of a person, the following results were obtained: Blue - Left 15, Right 85; Brown - Left 20, Right 80. Do these results indicate, at the 5% level of significance, an association between eye colour and left or right handedness?

Step 1: H0: eye colour and handedness are independent; H1: they are associated.

Row totals are 100 and 100, column totals are 35 (Left) and 165 (Right), n = 200.

Step 2: Expected frequencies are (100)(35) / 200 = 17.5 for each Left cell and (100)(165) / 200 = 82.5 for each Right cell.

Step 3: With Yates' correction for a 2 x 2 table, adjusted chi-square = sum of (|o - e| - 0.5)^2 / e = (2)^2 / 17.5 + (2)^2 / 82.5 + (2)^2 / 17.5 + (2)^2 / 82.5 = 0.55, about 0.56 as printed.

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (2 - 1)(2 - 1) = 1; critical value at 5% is 3.84. Since 0.56 < 3.84, we do not reject H0.

Answer: There is no association between eye colour and left or right handedness, as printed in the book.

Q. 1 (c) An investigation into colour-blindness and sex of a person gave the following results: Male - Colourblind 36, Not colourblind 964; Female - Colourblind 19, Not colourblind 981. Is there evidence, at the 5% level, of an association between the sex of a person and whether or not they are colourblind?

Step 1: H0: sex and colour-blindness are independent; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 1000 and 1000, column totals are 55 and 1945, n = 2000.

Step 2: Expected frequencies are (1000)(55) / 2000 = 27.5 for each Colourblind cell and (1000)(1945) / 2000 = 972.5 for each Not colourblind cell.

Step 3: With Yates' correction, adjusted chi-square = (8)^2 / 27.5 + (8)^2 / 972.5 + (8)^2 / 27.5 + (8)^2 / 972.5 = 4.79 as printed.

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = 1; critical value at 5% is 3.84. Since 4.79 > 3.84, we reject H0.

Answer: There is an association between sex of a person and colour-blindness, as printed in the book.

Q. 2 (a) A driving school examined the results of 100 candidates who were taking their driving test for the first time. They found that out of the 40 men, 28 passed and out of the 60 women, 34 passed. Do these results indicate, at the 5% level of significance, a relationship between the sex of a candidate and the ability to pass first time?

Step 1: Table: Men - Pass 28, Fail 12; Women - Pass 34, Fail 26. Column totals are 62 passed and 38 failed, n = 100.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Men-Pass (40)(62) / 100 = 24.8, Men-Fail (40)(38) / 100 = 15.2, Women-Pass (60)(62) / 100 = 37.2, Women-Fail (60)(38) / 100 = 22.8.

Step 3: With Yates' correction each |o - e| - 0.5 = 2.7, so adjusted chi-square = (2.7)^2 / 24.8 + (2.7)^2 / 15.2 + (2.7)^2 / 37.2 + (2.7)^2 / 22.8 = 1.29 as printed.

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = 1; critical value at 5% is 3.84. Since 1.29 < 3.84, we do not reject H0.

Answer: There is no relationship between the sex of a candidate and the ability to pass first time, as printed in the book.

Q. 2 (b) Out of 1350 persons, 450 were literate and 600 had traveled beyond the limits of their district, 300 of the literates were among those who had traveled. Find out by calculating (i) coefficient of association, (ii) the value of chi-square, if there is any association between traveling and literacy.

Step 1: Table: Literate and traveled = 300, Literate and not traveled = 150, Illiterate and traveled = 300, Illiterate and not traveled = 600.

Step 2 (i): Q = ((300)(600) - (150)(300)) / ((300)(600) + (150)(300)) = (180000 - 45000) / (180000 + 45000) = 135000 / 225000 = 0.6 as printed.

Step 3 (ii): Expected frequencies: (450)(600) / 1350 = 200, (450)(750) / 1350 = 250, (900)(600) / 1350 = 400, (900)(750) / 1350 = 500.

Step 4: With Yates' correction each |o - e| - 0.5 = 99.5, so adjusted chi-square = (99.5)^2 / 200 + (99.5)^2 / 250 + (99.5)^2 / 400 + (99.5)^2 / 500 = 133.65 as printed.

Step 5: Degrees of freedom = 1; critical value at 5% is 3.84. Since 133.65 > 3.84, we reject H0.

Answer: Q = 0.6 and adjusted chi-square = 133.65; there is an association between traveling and literacy, as printed in the book.

Q. 3 (a) The following are the data on a random sample of 150 chickens, divided into two groups according to breed and into three groups according to yield of eggs: Rhode Red - High 46, Medium 29, Low 28; Leghorn White - High 27, Medium 14, Low 6. Are these data consistent with the hypothesis that yield is not affected by the type of breed?

Step 1: H0: yield is not affected by breed (independence); H1: yield is affected by breed. Row totals are 103 and 47, column totals are 73, 43 and 34, n = 150.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Rhode Red - 50.13, 29.53, 23.35; Leghorn White - 22.87, 13.47, 10.65.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 4.07 as printed.

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (2 - 1)(3 - 1) = 2; critical value at 5% is 5.99. Since 4.07 < 5.99, we do not reject H0.

Answer: There is no association between chicken breed and yield of eggs, as printed in the book.

Q. 3 (b) The students of a college took three courses: arts, commerce and science.

The students were classified according to sex: Male - Arts 200, Commerce 300, Science 100; Female - Arts 100, Commerce 200, Science 100. Use chi-square test whether there is any association between sex and choice of course of study.

Step 1: H0: sex and choice of course are independent; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 600 and 400, column totals are 300, 500 and 200, n = 1000.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Male - 180, 300, 120; Female - 120, 200, 80.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 13.89 as printed (13.888).

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (2 - 1)(3 - 1) = 2; critical value at 5% is 5.99. Since 13.89 > 5.99, we reject H0.

Answer: There is an association between sex and course of study, as printed in the book.

Q. 4 (a) The following table shows liking of three colours: pink, white and blue in samples of males and females: Pink - Male 20, Female 40; White - Male 40, Female 20; Blue - Male 60, Female 20. Test whether there is any relation between sex and colour.

Step 1: H0: sex and liking of colours are independent; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 60, 60 and 80, column totals are 120 and 80, n = 200.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Pink - 36, 24; White - 36, 24; Blue - 48, 32.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 26.39 as printed (26.3889).

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(2 - 1) = 2; critical value at 5% is 5.99. Since 26.39 > 5.99, we reject H0.

Answer: There is a relation between sex and liking of colours, as printed in the book.

Q. 4 (b) The following table gives the condition at home and condition of the children: Clean - Clean 175, Not clean 143; Fairly clean - Clean 136, Not clean 116; Dirty - Clean 125, Not clean 145. Test for the association between the conditions at home and condition of children.

Step 1: H0: condition at home and condition of children are independent; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 318, 252 and 270, column totals are 436 and 404, n = 840.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Clean - 165.06, 152.94; Fairly clean - 130.80, 121.20; Dirty - 140.14, 129.86.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 5.08 by exact recomputation; the book prints 5.027, a small arithmetic difference that does not change the decision.

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(2 - 1) = 2; critical value at 5% is 5.99. Since 5.08 < 5.99, we do not reject H0.

Answer: There is no association between conditions at home and condition of children; the decision agrees with the book.

Q. 5 (a) The table given below shows the relation between the performance of students in economics and statistics. Test the hypothesis that the performance in economics is independent of the performance in statistics using 5% level of significance: Economics High - Statistics High 56, Medium 96, Low 28; Medium - High 48, Medium 168, Low 24; Low - High 16, Medium 86, Low 78.

Step 1: H0: performance in economics is independent of performance in statistics; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 180, 240 and 180, column totals are 120, 350 and 130, n = 600.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: High - 36, 105, 39; Medium - 48, 140, 52; Low - 36, 105, 39.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 89.21 as printed (89.2112).

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(3 - 1) = 4; critical value at 5% is 9.49. Since 89.21 > 9.49, we reject H0.

Answer: There is an association between the performance of students in economics and statistics, as printed in the book.

Q. 5 (b) A thousand households are taken at random and divided into three groups A, B and C, according to the total weekly income. The following table shows the numbers in each group having a colour television receiver, a black and white receiver, or no television at all: Colour television - A 56, B 51, C 93; Black and white - A 118, B 207, C 375; None - A 26, B 42, C 32. Calculate the expected frequencies if there is no association between total income and television ownership. Apply a test to find whether the observed frequencies suggest that there is such an association.

Step 1: Row totals are 200, 700 and 100; column totals are 200, 300 and 500; n = 1000.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Colour television - 40, 60, 100; Black and white - 140, 210, 350; None - 20, 30, 50.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 26.61 as printed (26.6).

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(3 - 1) = 4; critical value at 5% is 9.49. Since 26.61 > 9.49, we reject H0.

Answer: There is an association between television type and income group, as printed in the book.

Q. 6 (a) A random sample of 200 married men, all retired, were classified according to education and number of children as indicated below: Elementary - 0-1: 13, 2-3: 37, Over 3: 35; Secondary - 0-1: 19, 2-3: 42, Over 3: 14; College - 0-1: 12, 2-3: 17, Over 3: 11. Test the hypothesis, at 5% of significance, that the size of family is independent of the level of education attained by the father.

Step 1: H0: size of family is independent of the father's education; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 85, 75 and 40, column totals are 44, 96 and 60, n = 200.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: Elementary - 18.70, 40.80, 25.50; Secondary - 16.50, 36.00, 22.50; College - 8.80, 19.20, 12.00.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 11.72 as printed (11.7194).

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(3 - 1) = 4; critical value at 5% is 9.49. Since 11.72 > 9.49, we reject H0.

Answer: There is an association between education and number of children, as printed in the book.

Q. 6 (b) A survey of 200 families known to be regular television viewers was undertaken. They were asked which of the three television channels they watched most during an average week: PTV 1 - North 29, East 16, South 42, West 23; PTV 2 - North 6, East 11, South 26, West 7; STN - North 15, East 3, South 12, West 10. Test the hypothesis that there is no association between the channel watched most and the region.

Step 1: H0: channel watched and region are independent; H1: they are associated.

Row totals are 110, 50 and 40, column totals are 50, 30, 80 and 40, n = 200.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: PTV 1 - 27.50, 16.50, 44.00, 22.00; PTV 2 - 12.50, 7.50, 20.00, 10.00; STN - 10.00, 6.00, 16.00, 8.00.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 13.45 as printed (13.446).

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(4 - 1) = 6; critical value at 5% is 12.59. Since 13.45 > 12.59, we reject H0.

Answer: There is an association between the channel and region, as printed in the book.

Q. 6 (c) From the following table showing the number of employees and condition of factory premises: A1 - Under 50: 84, 51-150: 133, 151-250: 49, Over 250: 62; A2 - Under 50: 87, 51-150: 82, 151-250: 20, Over 250: 25; A3 - Under 50: 26, 51-150: 9, 151-250: 9, Over 250: 5. Discuss the association between the condition of premises and the number of persons employed. Compute the coefficient of contingency.

Step 1: H0: condition of premises and number of persons employed are independent; H1: they are associated. Row totals are 328, 214 and 49, column totals are 197, 224, 78 and 92, n = 591.

Step 2: Expected frequencies: A1 - 109.33, 124.32, 43.29, 51.06; A2 - 71.33, 81.11, 28.24, 33.31; A3 - 16.33, 18.57, 6.47, 7.63.

Step 3: Chi-square = sum of (o - e)^2 / e = 30.06 as printed.

Step 4: Degrees of freedom = (3 - 1)(4 - 1) = 6; critical value at 5% is 12.59. Since 30.06 > 12.59, we reject H0.

Step 5: Pearson's coefficient of mean square contingency C = sqrt(chi-square / (n + chi-square)) = sqrt(30.06 / (591 + 30.06)) = sqrt(30.06 / 621.06) = 0.22 as printed.

Answer: There is an association between the condition of premises and the number of persons employed, with C = 0.22.

mcqs.q: What is a cell frequency in a contingency table?
options: The total of one complete row
The total of one complete column
The number of observations in one particular row and column combination
The grand total n of the table
mcqs.why: The notes define the cell frequency as the frequency in any one cell, the number falling in one particular row and column combination.

mcqs.q: Eye colour and handedness: row totals 100 and 100, Left column total 35, n = 200. What is the expected frequency for each Left cell?
mcqs.why: Working: expected frequency = (row total x column total) / n = (100)(35) / 200 = 3500 / 200 = 17.5 for each Left cell.

mcqs.q: For eye colour and handedness the Yates-corrected chi-square is about 0.56 with 1 degree of freedom (critical value 3.84 at 5%). What is the conclusion?
options: Association exists, because degrees of freedom equal 1
No association, because n = 200 is small
mcqs.why: Working: 0.56 < 3.84, the 5% critical value, so H0 of independence is not rejected and there is no association.

mcqs.q: For sex and colour-blindness the Yates-corrected chi-square is 4.79 with critical value 3.84 at 5%. What is the conclusion?
options: No association, because 4.79 is close to 3.84
No association, because H0 is accepted
Association exists only if Q is also calculated
mcqs.why: Working: 4.79 > 3.84, the 5% critical value, so H0 is rejected and there is an association between sex and colour-blindness.

mcqs.q: Driving test: 40 men and 60 women, 62 passed in total. What is the expected frequency for Men-Pass?
mcqs.why: Working: expected frequency = (row total x column total) / n = (40)(62) / 100 = 2480 / 100 = 24.8 for the Men-Pass cell.

mcqs.q: Literacy and travel: (AB) = 300, (A beta) = 150, (alpha B) = 300, (alpha beta) = 600. What is the coefficient of association Q?
Chicken breed and egg yield (2 x 3 table): chi-square = 4.07, critical value at 5% is 5.99. What is the conclusion?
options: Yield is affected by breed, because chi-square is positive
Yield is affected by breed, because degrees of freedom equal 2
No conclusion is possible from chi-square alone
mcqs.why: Working: degrees of freedom = (2 - 1)(3 - 1) = 2 and 4.07 < 5.99, so H0 is not rejected; breed and yield are not associated.

mcqs.q: Sex and choice of course (2 x 3 table): chi-square = 13.89, critical value at 5% is 5.99. What is the conclusion?
options: Association exists only for the Arts course
mcqs.why: Working: degrees of freedom = (2 - 1)(3 - 1) = 2 and 13.89 > 5.99, so H0 is rejected; sex and course of study are associated.

mcqs.q: Home condition and children's condition: what chi-square value should be used, and what is the decision at 5% (critical value 5.99)?
mcqs.why: Working: exact recomputation gives chi-square = sum (o - e)^2 / e = 5.08; the book prints 5.027, a small arithmetic difference. Since 5.08 < 5.99, H0 is not rejected either way.

mcqs.q: Factory premises data: chi-square = 30.06 and n = 591. What is Pearson's coefficient of contingency C?
mcqs.why: Working: C = sqrt(chi-square / (n + chi-square)) = sqrt(30.06 / (591 + 30.06)) = sqrt(30.06 / 621.06) = sqrt(0.0484) = 0.22.

lessons.title: Exercise 15.3
lessons.notes_html:
Note: the book prints no Q. 2 in this exercise

Q. 1 (a) What is rank correlation?

Step 1: Rank correlation is the correlation between the ranks of individuals for two variables X and Y, instead of their measured values.

Step 2: When the observations are ranks, Spearman's coefficient of rank correlation is r_r = 1 - (6 sum of d_i squared) / (n (n squared - 1)), where d_i is the difference of the two ranks of the i-th individual.

Answer: It always lies between -1 and +1, and it is a nonparametric procedure that is useful when the basic data are not available in numerical form but only as ranks.

Q. 1 (b) The following table shows how 10 students, arranged in alphabetical order, were ranked according to their achievements in both laboratory and lecture portions of a statistics course. Find the coefficient of mark correlation: Laboratory ranks 8, 3, 9, 2, 7, 10, 4, 6, 1, 5; Lecture ranks 9, 5, 10, 1, 8, 7, 3, 4, 2, 6.

Step 1: Differences d = Laboratory rank - Lecture rank: -1, -2, -1, 1, -1, 3, 1, 2, -1, -1.

Step 2: Squares of d: 1, 4, 1, 1, 1, 9, 1, 4, 1, 1; sum of d squared = 24.

Step 3: r_r = 1 - (6)(24) / (10)(100 - 1) = 1 - 144 / 990 = 1 - 0.1455 = 0.8545.

Answer: r_r = 0.8545, as printed in the book.

Q. 1 (c) The ranks of the same 10 students in Mathematics and Economics were as follows: (1, 6); (2, 5); (3, 1); (4, 4); (5, 2); (6, 7); (7, 8); (8, 10); (9, 3); (10, 9); the two numbers within brackets denoting the ranks of the same students in Mathematics and Economics respectively. Calculate the rank correlation coefficient for proficiencies of this group in two subjects.

Step 1: Differences d = Mathematics rank - Economics rank: -5, -3, 2, 0, 3, -1, -1, -2, 6, 1.

Step 2: Squares of d: 25, 9, 4, 0, 9, 1, 1, 4, 36, 1; sum of d squared = 90.

Step 3: r_r = 1 - (6)(90) / (10)(100 - 1) = 1 - 540 / 990 = 1 - 0.5455 = 0.4545.

Answer: r_r = 0.45, as printed in the book (0.4545 rounded).

Q. 3 (a) Five sacks of coal A, B, C, D and E have different weights, with A being heavier than B, B being heavier than C, and so on. A weight lifter ranks the sacks (heaviest first) in the order A, D, B, E, C. Calculate a coefficient of rank correlation.

Step 1: True ranks (heaviest first): A 1, B 2, C 3, D 4, E 5. The lifter's ranks: A 1, B 3, C 5, D 2, E 4.

Step 2: Differences d = true rank - lifter's rank: A 0, B -1, C -2, D 2, E 1; squares 0, 1, 4, 4, 1; sum of d squared = 10.

Step 3: r_r = 1 - (6)(10) / (5)(25 - 1) = 1 - 60 / 120 = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5.

Answer: r_r = 0.5, as printed in the book.

Q. 3 (b) Seven army recruits A, B, C, D, E, F and G were given two separate aptitude tests. Their orders of merit in each test were: First test - G, F, A, D, B, C, E; Second test - D, F, E, B, G, C, A. Find Spearman's coefficient of rank correlation between the two orders and comment briefly on the correlation obtained.

Step 1: First-test ranks: A 3, B 5, C 6, D 4, E 7, F 2, G 1. Second-test ranks: A 7, B 4, C 6, D 1, E 3, F 2, G 5.

Step 2: Differences d = first - second: A -4, B 1, C 0, D 3, E 4, F 0, G -4; squares 16, 1, 0, 9, 16, 0, 16; sum of d squared = 58.

Step 3: r_r = 1 - (6)(58) / (7)(49 - 1) = 1 - 348 / 336 = 1 - 1.0357 = -0.0357.

Answer: r_r = -0.036, very little negative correlation, as printed in the book.

Q. 4 (a) Ten competitors in a beauty contest are ranked by three judges in the following order: Competitor A-J, Judge X: 1, 6, 5, 10, 3, 2, 4, 9, 7, 8; Judge Y: 3, 5, 8, 4, 7, 10, 2, 1, 6, 9; Judge Z: 6, 4, 9, 8, 1, 2, 3, 10, 5, 7. Use Spearman's rank correlation coefficient to discuss which pair of judges have the nearest approach to common tastes in beauty.

Step 1: For judges X and Y, differences d: -2, 1, -3, 6, -4, -8, 2, 8, 1, -1; squares 4, 1, 9, 36, 16, 64, 4, 64, 1, 1; sum = 200; r_xy = 1 - (6)(200) / (10)(99) = 1 - 1200 / 990 = -0.21.

Step 2: For judges Y and Z, differences d: -3, 1, -1, -4, 6, 8, -1, -9, 1, 2; squares 9, 1, 1, 16, 36, 64, 1, 81, 1, 4; sum = 214; r_yz = 1 - (6)(214) / 990 = 1 - 1284 / 990 = -0.30.

Step 3: For judges X and Z, differences d: -5, 2, -4, 2, 2, 0, 1, -1, 2, 1; squares 25, 4, 16, 4, 4, 0, 1, 1, 4, 1; sum = 60; r_xz = 1 - (6)(60) / 990 = 1 - 360 / 990 = 0.64.

Answer: r_xy = -0.21, r_yz = -0.30, r_xz = 0.64, as printed in the book. Judges X and Z have the nearest approach to common tastes in beauty, since their rank correlation is the largest positive value.

Q. 4 (b) The following table shows the grade point average awarded to six children in a competition by two different judges: Child A-F, Judge X: 6.8, 7.3, 8.1, 9.8, 7.1, 9.2; Judge Y: 7.8, 9.4, 7.9, 9.6, 8.9, 6.9. Calculate coefficient of rank correlation by Spearman's formula.

Step 1: Rank the averages from lowest to highest. Judge X ranks: A 1, B 3, C 4, D 6, E 2, F 5. Judge Y ranks: A 2, B 5, C 3, D 6, E 4, F 1.

Step 2: Differences d = X rank - Y rank: A -1, B -2, C 1, D 0, E -2, F 4; squares 1, 4, 1, 0, 4, 16; sum of d squared = 26.

Step 3: r_r = 1 - (6)(26) / (6)(36 - 1) = 1 - 156 / 210 = 1 - 0.7429 = 0.2571.

Answer: r_r = 0.26, as printed in the book.

Q. 4 (c) The following table shows the marks of six candidates in two subjects: Candidate A-F, Mathematics: 38, 62, 56, 42, 59, 48; Statistics: 64, 89, 84, 60, 73, 69. (i) Calculate the coefficient of rank correlation. (ii) Comment on the value of your result.

Step 1: Mathematics ranks (lowest to highest): A 1, B 6, C 4, D 2, E 5, F 3. Statistics ranks: A 2, B 6, C 5, D 1, E 4, F 3.

Step 2: Differences d = Mathematics rank - Statistics rank: A -1, B 0, C -1, D 1, E 1, F 0; squares 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0; sum of d squared = 4.

Step 3: r_r = 1 - (6)(4) / (6)(36 - 1) = 1 - 24 / 210 = 1 - 0.1143 = 0.8857.

Answer: (i) 0.886, as printed in the book. (ii) High positive correlation: candidates who rank high in Mathematics also rank high in Statistics.

mcqs.q: What is rank correlation?
options: Correlation between the measured values of X and Y
Correlation between the ranks of individuals for two variables X and Y
Association between two attributes in a 2 x 2 table
The discrepancy between observed and expected frequencies
mcqs.why: The notes define rank correlation as the correlation between the ranks of individuals for two variables X and Y, instead of their measured values.

mcqs.q: Which formula gives Spearman's coefficient of rank correlation r_r?
options: r_r = 1 - (6 sum of d_i squared) / (n (n squared - 1))
r_r = ((AB)(alpha beta) - (A beta)(alpha B)) / ((AB)(alpha beta) + (A beta)(alpha B))
r_r = sum of (o - e) squared / e
mcqs.why: The notes give Spearman's formula r_r = 1 - (6 sum d_i^2) / (n(n^2 - 1)), where d_i is the difference of the two ranks of the i-th individual.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Spearman's rank correlation is correct?
options: It always lies between 0 and 1 and needs numerical data
It always lies between -1 and +1 and is useful when data are only ranks
It is the same as Yule's coefficient Q
It can only be used for exactly 10 individuals
mcqs.why: The notes state r_r always lies between -1 and +1 and is a nonparametric procedure useful when data are available only as ranks.

mcqs.q: For 10 students the laboratory and lecture ranks give sum of d squared = 24. What is r_r?
For 10 students in Mathematics and Economics, sum of d squared = 90. What is the rank correlation coefficient?
Five coal sacks: true order A, B, C, D, E and the lifter's order A, D, B, E, C give sum of d squared = 10. What is r_r?
mcqs.why: Working: r_r = 1 - (6)(10) / (5)(25 - 1) = 1 - 60 / 120 = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5 for the lifter's ranking.

mcqs.q: Seven army recruits in two aptitude tests give sum of d squared = 58. What is Spearman's coefficient and its meaning?
mcqs.why: Working: r_r = 1 - (6)(58) / (7)(49 - 1) = 1 - 348 / 336 = 1 - 1.0357 = -0.0357, about -0.036, very little negative correlation.

mcqs.q: Beauty contest judges: r_xy = -0.21, r_yz = -0.30 and r_xz = 0.64. Which pair has the nearest approach to common tastes?
options: No pair, because two values are negative
mcqs.why: Working: r_xz = 1 - (6)(60) / 990 = 0.64 is the largest positive value, so judges X and Z have the nearest approach to common tastes.

mcqs.q: Six children graded by two judges give sum of d squared = 26 with n = 6. What is the coefficient of rank correlation?
Six candidates in Mathematics and Statistics give sum of d squared = 4 with n = 6. What is r_r and its interpretation?
mcqs.why: Working: r_r = 1 - (6)(4) / (6)(36 - 1) = 1 - 24 / 210 = 1 - 0.1143 = 0.8857, about 0.886, a high positive correlation.

lessons.title: Exercise 15.4 — Objective Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Note: book skips labels (xviii), (xix), (xxi)-(xxiii) in print

Note: 6 items already in the earlier block above

Q. 1 (i) A characteristic which varies in quantity from one individual to another is called a variable

Q. 1 (ii) A characteristic which varies in quality from one individual to another is called an attribute

Q. 1 (iii) The observations made on objects regarding an attribute are called qualitative data.

Q. 1 (iv) Dichotomy is a process of dividing the objects into two mutually exclusive classes of an attribute.

Q. 1 (v) The degree of linear relationship between the two variables is called correlation

Q. 1 (vi) The degree of relationship between the two attributes is called association

Q. 1 (vii) The two attributes A and B are independent , if (AB) = (A)(B) / n.

Q. 1 (viii) The two attributes A and B are associated , if (AB) is not equal to (A)(B) / n.

Q. 1 (ix) The two attributes A and B are positively associated, if (AB) > (A)(B) / n.

Q. 1 (x) The two attributes A and B are negatively associated, if (AB) < (A)(B) / n.

Q. 1 (xi) The coefficient of association, denoted by Q, is a measure of association between the two attributes

Q. 1 (xii) If the coefficient of association equals 0, the two attributes A and B are independent

Q. 1 (xiii) If the coefficient of association is not equal to 0, the two attributes A and B are associated

Q. 1 (xiv) If the coefficient of association equals -1, the two attributes A and B are completely dissociated

Q. 1 (xv) If the coefficient of association equals 1, the two attributes A and B are completely associated

Q. 1 (xvi) A contingency table consisting of r rows and c columns is made up of the observed frequencies relative to two attributes and their categories.

Q. 1 (xvii) The two attributes are said to be independent , if for every cell of a contingency table the observed frequency o-i-j is equal to expected frequency e-i-j.

Q. 1 (xx, as printed) For an r x c contingency table, the chi-squared-statistic has degrees of freedom v = (r - 1)(c - 1)

Q. 1 (xxiv, as printed) The larger are the difference between the observed and expected frequencies, the larger will be the value of chi-squared which leads to the rejection of H0 of independence.

Q. 2 (i) A characteristic which varies in quantity from one individual to another is called an attribute.

False

Q. 2 (ii) The quantitative data relating to an attribute may be obtained simply by noting its presence or absence in the objects.

True

True

True

False

True

Q. 2 (x) A contingency table consisting of r rows and c columns is made up of the observed frequencies relative to two attributes and their categories.

True

False

True
